title: Activity Web App
shortDescription: A full-stack activity tracking application built with React, TypeScript, and ASP.NET Core, featuring authenticated user-specific CRUD workflows and persistent relational data.
overview: Activity Web App is a full-stack application built to demonstrate how a modern frontend, REST API, authentication, and persistent data work together as one system. Authenticated users can create, view, update, and manage their own activities through a React interface backed by an ASP.NET Core API and SQLite database.
problem: I wanted to build a complete client-server application rather than an isolated frontend or API, with particular focus on authenticated workflows, persistent user-owned data, and clear separation between frontend and backend responsibilities.
solution: I built the frontend with React and TypeScript and connected it to an ASP.NET Core REST API. ASP.NET Core Identity handles user registration and authentication, while the backend exposes protected CRUD endpoints for activity data. SQLite provides relational persistence for both application and identity data, with activity operations scoped to the authenticated user.
outcome: The project demonstrates an end-to-end full-stack architecture covering frontend interaction, REST API design, authentication and authorization, user-scoped data access, relational persistence, and communication between independently structured client and server applications.
highlights: Built an end-to-end application with React and TypeScript backed by an ASP.NET Core REST API
Implemented user registration and authentication with ASP.NET Core Identity
Designed protected CRUD endpoints for user-specific activity data
Persisted application and identity data using SQLite
Separated frontend, API, authentication, and persistence concerns across a clear client-server architecture
